# Form controls and the field theme

## `MagicStarter.fieldTheme`

- `MagicStarterFieldTheme` sets the padding, minimum height and type of `MSInput`, `MSSelect`, `MSCombobox`, `MSSegmentedControl` and the `MagicStarterTimezoneSelect` trigger (the last three share `selectSizeClassName`). `useTheme()` resets it; `useWindTheme()` keeps a field you set.
- The input recipe is `buildInputRecipe(theme)`; `selectRecipe`, `comboboxRecipe` and `segmentedControlRecipe` take `theme:`, which the widgets fill from the facade.
- Each field replaces one run of tokens in its recipe, so the side padding (`px-3`), the colours and the border stay outside it, and a host string states the whole size. The placeholder inherits the field's type, so there is no placeholder field.
- The default theme emits the previous classNames byte for byte (tests pin them), with one exception: the input's `text-fg` moved ahead of the size run (`px-3 text-fg py-3 lg:py-2.5 text-sm leading-5`) so the run is contiguous, which parses to the same style.
- A caller `className` or `classNames` is appended after the theme and wins.

## 44 px per control

- 44 px is padding around a fixed `leading-*`, and the numbers differ per control: `WInput` paints its border inside the padding (`py-[11px]` around 22 is 44, `py-2.5` is 42), while a `WSelect` trigger adds it (`py-2.5` is 44).
- `MSSegmentedControl` needs `segmentedPaddingClassName: 'px-1 py-0 lg:py-1'` for a 44 px control below `lg`, where the 44 px hit cell plus the default `p-1` root is 52 px. The `hit` slot is the touch target and is never themed.
- The auth, profile and settings forms use `WFormInput` on `formTheme.inputClassName` (its own `py-3`) and sit outside this theme, as do the starter's own `WFormSelect`s (team settings role, profile language, language preference), whose trigger reads the same string. One `py-*` cannot make both 44 px; `py-[10px] min-h-11 text-[17px] leading-[22px]` does.

## `MSSegmentedControl` reveal

- It is a `StatefulWidget` only for the reveal: on first mount and when `selectedIndex` changes, after the frame, it calls `position.ensureVisible` with `keepVisibleAtEnd` then `keepVisibleAtStart` on the scroller nearest to the segment (`Scrollable.maybeOf(segment)`, any axis), keyed by one `GlobalKey` per segment. A rebuild with the same `selectedIndex` reveals nothing, so the user's own scrolling stays.
- It moves only a horizontal scroller that is the root's own (`overflow-x-auto`) or has the control as its whole content (`maxScrollExtent + viewportDimension` within 1 px of the control's width). A strip with padding or a sibling is the host's and is left alone; moving it would snap a page view mid-drag.
- Not `Scrollable.maybeOf(segment, axis: Axis.horizontal)`: it skips a vertical list in between, and `ensureVisible` then measures against that list's viewport and jumps its vertical offset.
- Not `Scrollable.ensureVisible`: it walks every scrollable above the segment, so the page's vertical scroll view would jump to the control.
